# `css-modules/no-unused-class`

**A CSS Module class is read somewhere**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-css-modules` (npm) |
| **Languages** | CSS, SCSS |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:css-modules/recommended` at `warn` · `codelaw:css-modules/strict` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `warn` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (a class can be read by a name built at run time or by code outside the repo, so deleting its rule needs a person to accept the diff) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |
| **Scope** | project — reads the whole repository through the project graph, not one file at a time |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-css-modules/no-unused-class` |

## What it checks

Every class a CSS Module defines is read by a JavaScript or TypeScript file that imports the module: `styles.name`, `styles["name"]`, `const { name } = styles`, `import { name } from "./x.module.css"`, or composed by another class with `composes`.

**Why:** a class nobody reads is dead CSS that every page downloads, and it hides the classes the component really uses.

A module is left alone when any importer reads it by a computed name (`styles[name]`, `styles[\`btn-${size}\`]`), spreads it, or passes it to a function: the rule cannot tell which classes that reaches, so it reports none rather than guess. A module no file imports is left alone too.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-css-modules
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:css-modules/recommended` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:css-modules/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"css-modules/no-unused-class" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.css"]
rules = { "css-modules/no-unused-class" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"css-modules/no-unused-class" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"css-modules/no-unused-class" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"css-modules/no-unused-class" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "css-modules/no-unused-class": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Also configured by `[css]`

CSS Modules: which stylesheets are modules, and how the bundler turns a class name into `styles.x`. Read by the `css-modules/*` rules and the project graph. Root config only.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `modules` | `array` | `[]` | Globs of CSS Module stylesheets besides `*.module.css` and `*.module.scss`, from the project root. |
| `modules_convention` | `asIs` · `camelCase` · `camelCaseOnly` · `dashes` · `dashesOnly` | `"asIs"` | css-loader's `localsConvention`: how a class such as `.btn-primary` is reached from JavaScript. `asIs`: `styles["btn-primary"]`; `camelCase`: that and `styles.btnPrimary`; `camelCaseOnly`: only `styles.btnPrimary`; `dashes` and `dashesOnly`: dashes become camel case, other characters stay. |

```toml
[css]
modules = ["src/**/*.styles.css"]
modules_convention = "camelCase"
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **CSS:** `/* codelaw-ignore css-modules/no-unused-class: <reason> */`
- **SCSS:** `// codelaw-ignore css-modules/no-unused-class: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `/* codelaw-ignore css-modules/no-unused-class expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason> */`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule css-modules/no-unused-class --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain css-modules/no-unused-class       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule css-modules/no-unused-class  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>               # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Search for the class: `styles.name`, a bracket access, and any `composes` that names it.
2. If a component builds the name at run time, read it by a plain `styles.name` somewhere, or accept that this module is dynamic.
3. Otherwise delete the rule (`codelaw fix --unsafe` does it when the class is the rule's only selector).

## Examples

### CSS

#### Don't

```css files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.legacy { color: red; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

#### Do

```css files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss files
/* src/Card.module.scss */
$gap: 1rem;
.card { padding: $gap; }
.legacy { color: red; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.scss";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

#### Do

```scss files
/* src/Card.module.scss */
$gap: 1rem;
.card { padding: $gap; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.scss";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

## Differences from the source

eslint-plugin-css-modules's `no-unused-class` reads one JS file against its stylesheet; this rule reads the project, so a module imported from several files is judged by all of them, `composes` counts as a use, and a computed access silences the module (the plugin's `camelCase` option is `[css] modules_convention`).
